subject: Cardinal AI evaluation materials: escrow, usage gates, and close cadence
messages:
From: Amy Torres <amy.torres@cardinal.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Cardinal AI Procurement <procure@cardinal.ai>
Date: Mon, 7 Mar 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cardinal evaluation — initial material drop and MAP proposal

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Per our conversation, attached are the initial artifacts for the evaluation: a trimmed dataset (Cardinal_eval_dataset_v1.zip) and a prompt pack used in our internal QA (PromptPack_Cardinal_v2.pdf). We’ve also sketched a short MAP (attached as MAP_Cardinal-RDW-8421.xlsx) that ties the data delivery to two acceptance gates: (1) model-level quality checks run on your side, and (2) a short functional QA pass with our product team.

Key constraints from our side:
- All assets are under an evaluation-only license (30 days) and must be destroyed or returned after the window unless we agree to an extension.
- No transfer to third parties; sandbox only.
- Outputs derived from the dataset should not be used for model training or benchmarking outside the scope of the acceptance checks.

Ask: Can Redwood confirm the escrow and takedown process (who will attest to deletion) and an internal contact for legal to sync on the single-page limited-use clause? We’re aiming to start the MAP on 2027-03-09 and close by 2027-04-08 if the acceptance gates are met.

Attachments:
- Cardinal_eval_dataset_v1.zip (attachment stub)
- PromptPack_Cardinal_v2.pdf (attachment stub)
- MAP_Cardinal-RDW-8421.xlsx (attachment stub)

Thanks,
Amy Torres
Head of Partnerships | Cardinal AI
amy.torres@cardinal.ai
+1 415-555-0123
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: Amy Torres <amy.torres@cardinal.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Mar 2027 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cardinal evaluation — initial material drop and MAP proposal

Amy —

Appreciate the materials and the clear constraints. I reviewed the MAP briefly and the plan is reasonable. Quick answers to your asks:

- Escrow/takedown: Redwood can host the artifacts in an ephemeral sandbox in our Dedicated partner corridor. At the end of the 30-day window, our platform will produce a tamper-evident deletion report and a checksum-based attest (we'll provide an export to your legal team).
- Legal sync: looping in Ben (sales lead) and Laura (program owner) on this thread to coordinate the limited-use language and operational playbook.

Proposed operational updates before we kick off:
1) Add a short living list of testcases we will run against the model (we'll share a draft testset by EOD 3/8).
2) Permit-cardinality: allow one short extension (up to +14 days) if both parties agree; any further extension requires exec approval.
3) Logging: we will enable request-level tracing for the acceptance window, retained for 30 days and then purged unless otherwise requested by you.

If that matches Cardinal's expectations I’ll have Laura send a 1-page onboarding checklist and Ben will follow up on contractual language for the single-page limited-use rider.

-Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Partner Ops | Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwoodinference.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Amy Torres <amy.torres@cardinal.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Mar 2027 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Cardinal evaluation — initial material drop and MAP proposal

Amy — quick follow-up from legal and commercial:

We can accept the 30-day ephemeral evaluation license with a single +14 day extension as Markus suggested. A couple of small redlines we’ll propose in the single-page rider:
- Clarify that "derivative outputs" excludes ephemeral inference logs used for acceptance checks, but still prohibits persistent incorporation into training corpora.
- Add a clause that Redwood’s deletion attestation is considered sufficient unless Cardinal specifically requests a joint audit (we can accommodate but it will add 3–5 business days).

Next steps I propose:
- Laura to send the onboarding checklist (ops) and the draft testcases for your review by EOD 3/8.
- I’ll upload a one-page rider to the HubSpot deal record and send a DocuSign link for Cardinal's procurement if this aligns.

Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales Lead | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
+1 650-555-0199

Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Cardinal evaluation — onboarding checklist, testcases, and kickoff cadence

Hi Amy —

Thanks for the materials and patience while we pulled the drafts together. Attached are: Redwood-Eval-Onboarding-Checklist.docx and a short draft testset (Testset_Cardinal_v1.txt) outlining the 12 acceptance checks we'll run (functional, safety smoke tests, and a handful of high-priority generative prompts you provided).

Operational cadence we propose:
- 2027-03-09: Ephemeral sandbox provisioned and artifacts ingested.
- 2027-03-10 to 2027-03-16: Redwood runs acceptance testset against our staging model; we share a first-pass results report on 3/17.
- 2027-03-18 to 2027-03-22: Cardinal QA performs the functional pass in the sandbox (we'll provide a dedicated workspace and access lanes).
- 2027-03-24: Joint acceptance review call; decision to close or trigger single +14d extension.
- 2027-04-08: Rollback/takedown complete if acceptance passed and no extension taken.

Please confirm the timeline or propose any adjustments. Ben will send the one-page rider via DocuSign once we have confirmation on the timeline and the single-page limited-use language.

Attachments referenced:
- Redwood-Eval-Onboarding-Checklist.docx (attachment stub)
- Testset_Cardinal_v1.txt (attachment stub)

Best,
Laura Bennett
